title: Reduce GPU memory: activation checkpointing, scratch buffers, and arena tuning
author: Ariel Kim
description: Motivation: production workloads running on constrained GPU instances were hitting OOMs due to recent model size increases and peak workspace allocations from certain kernels. This PR reduces GPU resident memory and peak workspace requirements through three complementary changes: (1) enable optional activation checkpointing at the model shard/runtime layer with a heuristic that targets long transformer blocks; (2) implement a scratch-buffer pooling allocator to reuse per-request temporary buffers across kernels instead of allocating per-kernel; (3) tune the arena allocator defaults (smaller initial arena, upper bounds on arena growth) and expose configuration knobs to operators. The description below summarizes the implementation, safety checks, benchmark results, and rollout plan.

ci_summary: Initial CI run flagged a flaky GPU memory profiling test (integration/gpu_memory_profile). After stabilizing the test harness and re-running, all checks passed: unit tests, integration tests on GPU, lint, and performance smoke tests. Benchmarks attached to the PR comment (see bench hashes).
benchmarks: Synthetic perf runs on p3.2xlarge and g5.xlarge types. Peak GPU memory reduced by 20-35% depending on model shape (longer seq lengths see larger wins). End-to-end latency impact: median latency regression <1.5% in steady-state; 95th percentile unchanged for typical route configs. Throughput improved by ~5% in continuous-batching scenarios due to lower OOM / fewer evictions. See bench artifacts: bench/run-2024-11-25-1 (p3) and bench/run-2024-11-26-1 (g5).
safety_and_rollout: Feature gates: runtime.checkpointing.enabled (global default=false), runtime.checkpointing.heuristic.threshold_blocks, allocator.scratch_pool.enabled (default=true but configurable), allocator.arena.max_mb. Rollout plan: deploy to staging with metric collection for one week, enable for a small subset of customers (canary 1%) using per-route config, monitor allocator.scratch_pool.fallback_count and latency SLOs, then ramp to 100% if stable. Revert: quick rollback by flipping flags via control plane. Added a canary regression alert (SLO alert rule) if 95th latency increases >10% or fallback_count spikes.
release_notes:
- Reduced GPU peak memory usage (20-35%) via activation checkpointing heuristics, scratch buffer pooling, and arena allocator tuning.
- Exposed runtime config knobs: runtime.checkpointing.enabled, allocator.scratch_pool.enabled, allocator.arena.max_mb.
- No breaking API changes.
notes_for_oncall: If customers report increased tail latency after rollout, check allocator.scratch_pool.fallback_count and runtime.checkpointing.enabled per-route. If fallback_count is high, consider increasing scratch_pool.initial_mb or disable scratch_pool for the affected deployment. For OOM escalations, use control plane flag to disable checkpointing per-customer.
notes: This PR consolidates and generalizes several prior optimizations; it aims to be conservative (opt-in checkpointing, safe allocator fallbacks) to minimize customer impact. CI artifacts and perf logs are attached in the PR comments.
